\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{сын} (syn)}{сын (syn)}]{\ru{сын} (syn) — a son}

\label{lesson:RU-C35-son}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for sadness, then the Russian for tiredness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{сын}}
\textbf{\ru{сын}} (\emph{syn}) — \textquotedblleft{}a son\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{сын}} $\leftarrow$ Proto-Slavic \emph{*synŭ} — inherited from PIE \emph{*suHnús}, \textquotedblleft{}son\textquotedblright{}. Vasmer lists Lithuanian \emph{sūnùs}, Sanskrit \emph{sūnú-} and Gothic \emph{sunus}, so English \emph{son} is a cousin, and he links the word with a Sanskrit verb \textquotedblleft{}to give birth\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{syn}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{syn}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Russian for sadness, then the Russian for tiredness, then say \emph{syn} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{бабушка} (bábushka)}{бабушка (bábushka)}]{\ru{бабушка} (bábushka) — a grandmother}

\label{lesson:RU-C35-grandmother}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for a son, then the Russian for a daughter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{бабушка}}
\textbf{\ru{бабушка}} (\emph{bábushka}) — \textquotedblleft{}a grandmother\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{бабушка}} is \emph{\ru{баба}}, \textquotedblleft{}old woman, granny\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{-\ru{ушка}}, a fond diminutive. \emph{\ru{баба}} is a nursery word, says Vasmer, and Lithuanian \emph{bóba}, \textquotedblleft{}old woman\textquotedblright{}, is the same kind of word.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{муж} (muzh)}{муж (muzh)}]{\ru{муж} (muzh) — a husband}

Before the new one: say the Russian for a daughter, then the Russian for a grandmother.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{муж}}
\textbf{\ru{муж}} (\emph{muzh}) — \textquotedblleft{}a husband\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ru{муж}} $\leftarrow$ Proto-Slavic \emph{*mǫžĭ}, \textquotedblleft{}a man\textquotedblright{} — inherited. \end{cousinweb}
